Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 103, verses 1–3 (part 1 of 3)

The question is: what is faith (iman)? .... We do not give a jurisprudential (fiqhi) explanation or definition of faith here. Our discussion is limited to the temperament of faith, its worth and value, and its effects on life.

Faith is in fact the bond that this small, limited, human creature establishes with the Reality that is eternal, everlasting and enduring, which is the origin of this universe and from which this universe came into existence. For this reason, this human creature is also connected to the universe, in that both have one Creator. Then this human being is connected to the laws of nature according to which this world operates, and the human being is connected to the forces that are active in this universe. The human being steps out of the shell of his own petty and limited self and enters into the vastness of the universe. Thus he goes beyond the boundaries of his limited power and enters the "limitless powers" that exist within this universe. This universe is so vast in comparison to the human being that its very boundaries lie beyond human knowledge. Then the human being steps out of the circle of his limited lifespan and enters the limitless times of the existence and the times that come after the Resurrection.

This bond of human creation, which grants strength, vastness and freedom, also grants him the taste to enjoy this entire universe and the beauty found within it, and to see the creatures that love his soul. Because of this bond, the brief journey of life becomes a journey of recreation for the human being, or becomes a tour of an exhibition that Allah has adorned for this human being in every place, every location and every era. The truth is that this is a very great good fortune, a supreme level of joy and recreation, and a friendship with this entire universe. It is a wealth compared to which no other wealth has any value. It is also a loss such that if someone is deprived of it, there is no greater loss or deficit than that.

Furthermore, the basic elements of faith are also those that are the basic constituent elements of humanity:

(1) Through the servitude of one God, a person is freed from all obedience, servitude and worship other than the One God. In this way, a sense arises within people that all servants have one standing and are equal with one another. Therefore, it is not a reasonable attitude that a person should be granted the true blessing of freedom! This is the freedom that springs from the human conscience and springs from the concept that exists as a fact and reality, and that concept is that in this universe there is only one real power and one real object of worship. Accordingly, the natural demand of this conception of life and conception of the universe is that the human being be free, and the logical outcome of this belief is also that the human being be free.

(2) A person develops Rabbaniyyah (a state of being devoted to the Lord), and he derives all his concepts, all his values and standards, all his priorities, and his entire constitution and law from Allah. His relations with Allah, with this universe, and with people are established in accordance with Allah's commands and laws. His personal desires and personal interests disappear from his life, and in their place Allah's Shariah (law) and justice take over. In the consciousness of the believer, the worth and value of his system of life rises, and his personality is elevated above the concepts and values of Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance, pre-Islamic paganism). Jahili priorities come to an end, and all the bonds that are based on the earth, this world and material concepts come to an end. Even if this person is an individual, because a believing individual also takes his concepts, his values and his priorities directly from Allah, since these values are indeed more exalted, more honourable, and more beneficial and deserving of regard.

(3) As a result of faith, the relationship between the Creator and the creation is also determined. The station of divinity and servitude, of lordship and bondage, is also determined, and this relationship comes forth clear and pure. This relationship, which connects a mortal human being to an immortal Being, is determined and made clear in a very simple and understandable manner, and in this path the human being no longer needs any intermediary. Through the clarification of ranks, light arises in the heart and tranquility in the soul. Love and trust arise in the human self. Anxiety, fear, distress and restlessness come to an end. Through this clarity of ranks, a person neither commits unjust arrogance, nor, by fabricating falsehoods and relying on invented concepts, claims for himself a superior station over other human beings.

(4) Because of faith, the People of Faith are granted steadfastness upon the Islamic system of life. Therefore, goodness among believers is not a temporary matter, nor an accidental, isolated incident. Rather, the Islamic system is an event that has real causes and has certain real objectives, and those who run the Islamic system are people bound together fi Allah (for the sake of Allah), who support one another. From such people a sound community is formed, which has one single purpose and one distinguished banner. This community is a historical community, and its past generations are also connected to the coming generations, and the coming generations are connected to the past, and this connection is a strong connection.

(5) As a result of this, a concept arises among people that the human being is extremely honoured. The human being rises in his own eyes, and in the conscience of the believer there is established the modesty that he should not do any action as a result of which he would fall from the rank to which Allah has raised him. This is that exalted and lofty station which no human being could even imagine reaching, that he is honoured in the sight of Allah. Every religion or philosophical concept that lowers a human being in his own eyes and declares him to be a contemptible creature, which was created in a manner that is regarded as a later addition, actually creates a distance between the human being and the higher realm. Such a religion or philosophy lowers the human being and leads him towards degradation, even if it does not say this explicitly.

Thus, the philosophies of Darwin and Freud and the Marxist system were the worst philosophies and systems, which afflicted humanity with the worst calamity and gave it a wrong direction from the standpoint of humanity, human nature and humanity itself, and made it believe that every degradation, every filth and every contempt is in fact a natural and necessary part of human life. This is not something to be surprised at, and therefore there is nothing to be ashamed of in it. Thus these philosophies and systems are in fact a heinous crime against humanity and deserve to be hated. (Sayyid, are you not aware that all the idols of Marxism have been toppled from the socialist world?)

(6) The mere concept that a human being is an honoured creature in the sight of Allah purifies and cleanses human consciousness. Then the concept that Allah is the Overseer of all, and that He knows what is in the breasts, also purifies human consciousness. A sound-natured human being, whose nature has not been distorted by the writings of people like Karl Marx and Freud, is ashamed that another human being like himself should become aware of the secrets of his heart and his evil thoughts. And a true believer, who holds the conviction that Allah is aware of all the secrets and hidden things in his breast, trembles at the thought that these and these thoughts exist in his heart. Through this he cleanses his consciousness and his feelings, and also purifies his heart.

The truth is that the moment faith arises, a moral beauty arises within the human being. He believes that there is one God who is just, merciful, generous and forgiving, forbearing and loving. He does not like evil, He likes goodness. He knows the treachery of the eyes and is the Knower of the secrets of hearts.

(7) Then there is the concept that the human being has been granted freedom of will, and at the same time he is being fully observed by Allah. As a result, awareness and alertness arise within the person, and the understanding and reflection that arise from this lead the human being to adopt a responsible attitude, both regarding himself and regarding other human beings. This responsibility is before Allah. Therefore, when a believer performs any action, his awareness and consciousness is that in every matter and at every step he thinks in his heart and considers the consequences before taking a step. This is because, according to this concept, the human being is a creature who has a position in this world. Therefore, within the order of this universe he is a responsible creature.

(8) Among the important effects of faith is that a believer does not pounce upon the interests of this world in the way that dogs pounce upon bones. Among the indications and effects of faith is that it leads a person to choose that which has lofty purpose in the sight of Allah, and which is "good" and enduring.

﴿And for this let the competitors compete﴾ (26:83). "Let those who wish to compete compete in goodness." Competition in the rewards that are with Allah lifts a person above this world, purifies his heart, and the person becomes clean and pure. Moreover, through this the sphere of a believer's activities becomes broader. He goes beyond the borders of this world and is active in the Hereafter as well. Alongside the earth, he also displays his vigour in the higher realm. This very thing creates in him the strength to continue doing good without concern for results, or not to be hasty about results. This is because he seeks goodness because it is goodness, and because the will of Allah is such. It is not his responsibility that the results of goodness should emerge within this small, limited lifespan. This is because the Allah for whose sake this goodness is being done is Living; He does not die. He does not forget, and He is not unaware of anything. Furthermore, this world is not the true abode of recompense, and all accounts are not settled in this world alone. Therefore, the believer seeks help to keep goodness flowing from a spring that never dries up, and this is why the movement of goodness continues. This is not a momentary enthusiasm, nor an individual incident. It is this faithful spirit which creates in a believer such strength that he stands up against the greatest of evils, whether this evil takes the form of a single dictator and tyrant, or the pressure of Jahili concepts and priorities, or the form of the desires of the self. This individual pressure falls upon a person in such a way that he thinks that this world is brief, that life is short, and that one should indulge in pleasures within it:

"Babur, live in pleasure, for the world is not repeated." (Babur ba-aish kosh, ki alam dobara nist.)

Or he thinks that it is so brief that good deeds cannot bear their results within it, and that we do not see any chance of seeing the triumph of truth over falsehood. Therefore faith treats this condition, and treats it at its very root.

The truth is that faith alone is the foundation of life and the root of life, and from it all the branches of goodness spring forth, and every fruit of it hangs from these roots. If faith is absent, it is as if the root of a tree has been cut, and all its branches will wither and dry up. And if they do not dry up, then they will be a satanic fruit, and it will not attain permanence or growth.

The truth is that faith is the centre and axis to which all the strings of a higher life are connected, and if faith is absent, life becomes a disconnected movement, and without faith this life has no stability or repose. Desires and inclinations pull a person wherever they go, carrying him away.

Faith is in fact a system, and because of it all the scattered deeds become connected with one another, and because of it these deeds come into harmony with one another. They come to be in one direction, having one movement, one motive, and one target.

It is for this reason that the Holy Quran declares null and void every deed that is not based upon this principle, that does not revolve around this axis, and that does not spring from the fountainhead of faith. The Islamic ideology of life and the Islamic system of beliefs are completely open and explicit in this matter. In Surah Ibrahim it is said:

﴿The likeness of those who disbelieved in their Lord is that their deeds are like ashes, which the wind blows violently on a stormy day. They will not be able to obtain anything of what they have earned﴾ (18:14). And in Surah Nur it is said:

﴿As for those who disbelieved, their deeds are like a mirage in a level desert, which the thirsty one thinks to be water, until when he comes to it he finds it to be nothing﴾ (39:24).

These texts clearly indicate that deeds, as long as they are not based upon faith, have no worth or value in Islam. Beneath deeds there must be the motive that the Creator of the universe has commanded them, and their purpose must be to be in harmony with the creation of this universe. This is the logical outcome of the belief that returns all matters to Allah. Therefore, any deed that has been severed from faith loses its meaning and value.

(Ustad Muhammad Abduh, under the verse ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ (8:99), wrote: "Some scholars have recorded a consensus (ijma') that no good deed of a disbeliever will benefit him on the Day of Resurrection, and his punishment will not be lightened; but this is a fundamental matter." We believe that this question is not one of consensus, but one of the explicit texts of the Quran, and the Quran and Sunnah are completely clear in this matter.) (Sayyid Qutb)

**Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran) on Surah 103, verses 1–3 (part 2 of 3)**

Faith is evidence that the believer's nature is sound, the structure of his personality is intact and whole, and he moves in harmony with this entire universe. The natural order that exists in his environment is in accord with him, and therefore he lives within this universe. Every believer whose personality is sound has a harmony with the universe, and this harmony and unity is the fruit of faith alone. The universe contains signs and indications that show that one and the same hand of power is the Creator of the cosmos. Therefore, if this harmony between a person and the universe is broken, it is evidence that his personality has been disturbed and that the capacity by which he draws lessons and signs from the universe has been lost. Because of this corruption, the person will remain in loss. Even if some of his deeds appear to bear the mark of goodness, without faith these deeds will not be accepted.... In short, the world of the believer is broad, comprehensive, long-reaching, elevated, beautiful and successful. In contrast, the world of those who are not believers is small, base, low, weak, hopeless and wretched, and its outcome and end is loss and failure.

﴿And do righteous deeds﴾ (3:103). Righteous deeds are in truth the natural fruit of faith. When faith settles in a heart, righteous action becomes its inherent movement, just as the heart is in constant motion. Faith is therefore a dynamic and positive movement. As soon as it takes its seat in a personality, it appears in the form of righteous action. From the Islamic point of view, faith is exactly like this. Islam does not recognize a faith that is extinguished and produces no movement, a faith that is hidden and does not come out of the believer's being in living form. If there is no such natural movement within it, that faith is counterfeit and dead. Faith is a flower whose fragrance cannot be stopped; wherever there is a flower, its fragrance will continue to spread. And if a person has no scent of faith, it is as though he does not exist.

From this it becomes clear that faith is the name of movement, action and construction, and all these matters come from Allah. Faith contains no contraction; it is not a negative thing. It does not settle in the hidden folds of the conscience. Faith is not the name of good wishes that are not backed by any movement. This is the open temperament of Islam, which makes Islam a superior constructive force, and this power is the central driving force within practical life.

This is the meaning of the principle that faith must be connected with the Islamic system of life. The Islamic system of life is a continuous movement that is taking place throughout this entire universe. This movement has been created by a governing power, it has a purpose, and handing leadership of humanity to faith means bringing into being a leadership that establishes a method of movement in accordance with the temperament of this entire universe. In other words, it means establishing a good, pure and constructive struggle that is worthy of the system of life that has come from Allah.

﴿And who enjoin one another to truth and enjoin one another to patience﴾ (3:103). Through the acts of enjoining truth and enjoining patience, the features of the Muslim ummah (community) become clearly visible. The organized community (jama'ah muslimah) is also established along the lines of the Muslim ummah. It has a distinct existence and personality. Its members have a distinctive bond among them. All people share one direction. This ummah or community is also conscious of its own existence, and its duties are before it. This ummah knows what it must do in relation to faith and righteous action. It knows that from the standpoint of faith and righteous action it must also lead all of humanity. Therefore, to counsel one another to truth means that you must rise up carrying the Great Trust (amanat kubra).

In short, from the word "tawasi" (mutual counsel and exhortation), and from its meaning, its character and its reality, the existence of the Muslim ummah emerges, or the concept of a united community arises. That is, an ummah that is distinguished, wise, and responsible for establishing truth, goodness, and justice upon this earth. Thus this is the most sublime and beautiful picture of the Muslim ummah. Islam desires such an ummah: a distinguished, strong, wise community that watches over truth and goodness, whose members constantly counsel one another to truth and exhort one another to patience, live together in love and cooperation, and among whom a special brotherhood prevails, which the Qur'an expresses as mutual counsel.

Enjoining truth is necessary because carrying the truth is a difficult task. In this world there are countless factors that lead a person away from the path of truth: carnal desires, expediency, national and family notions, the oppression of rebels and dictators, the injustice of wrongdoers, the transgressions of those who exceed limits, and so on. When people counsel one another, in essence a reminder takes place. People's resolve grows, and in terms of aims and objectives, unity and oneness arise among the members of the community. And in taking up responsibilities, in essence one bears the burden of another. Through counsel, all individual tendencies are gathered together and multiplied many times over, and those who are the guardians and supporters of truth feel that they are not alone. In the work of protecting truth and reality, there are others with me. They counsel him, encourage him, love him, and stand behind him, and they will never let him be humiliated. This religion is indeed the truth, and only a community can protect this religion, one that is mutually known, mutually responsible, mutually supportive, and that makes up for one another's weaknesses.

Enjoining patience is also very necessary, because remaining on the path of faith and righteous action and watching over truth and justice is a difficult task. It requires patience, perseverance, and fierce struggle against the factors within the self, and it also requires struggle against the factors outside the self. It requires endurance and hardship in the face of difficulties that arise on this path. Likewise, it requires patience in the face of the arrogance and pride of falsehood, patience over the length of the road, patience over the slowness of success, and patience when the signs of the path become obscure and vanish.

Enjoining patience increases human strength and produces a collective consciousness among people, that all of us have one goal and one direction. In this way everyone receives support. Workers, while laboring on this path, become close and intimate with one another, and they advance with great determination, steadfastness, and insistence upon their aim. Furthermore, through this several other collective qualities also come into being, and these are necessary for the stability of the Islamic community, because Islam cannot live without a communal atmosphere. Islam also manifests itself in the form of a society. If there is no society, there will be no Islam, and that would be sheer loss.

The Qur'an has established for us a constitution according to which a society is declared successful and protected from worldly and otherworldly loss. If we examine the present condition of the world through the lens of this constitution, we will see before us this frightful picture of the world: that the whole world is at present in complete loss. The more frightening aspect of this loss is that, even before the Hereafter, we have already fallen into severe loss from a purely worldly standpoint. We see that humanity has completely turned away from that goodness whose blessings Allah had made universal for mankind. Furthermore, that sovereign authority which is faithful and Islamic, which is founded upon goodness and the principles of truth and justice, has disappeared from this world. The most ugly aspect of this picture is that Muslims, or more precisely, those people who were far from goodness and virtue in comparison with other human beings who dwell on this earth, have moved far away from the system of life that Allah had chosen for them. They have trampled underfoot the constitution and law that Allah had prescribed for them, which Allah had declared to be the only path to salvation from loss and failure. Especially those lands from which the banners of goodness were first raised have themselves brought down the banners that Allah had raised for them. These were the banners of faith. And the most unfortunate thing is that the lands from which the banners of Allah's religion were raised have adopted racial nationalism, although the history of this earth bears witness that no people has ever attained goodness through racial nationalism. The nationalism (Arab nationalism) whose banners these people have raised existed before Islam as well, but because of it they neither accomplished any notable achievement on this earth, nor was any achievement of theirs recorded in the heavens. When Islam came, through the Arabs it raised a banner that was purely the banner of Allah. No other element shared in it. It was in the name of Allah, and no one shared in that name. It was attributed only to Allah, with no other attribution. It bore only the color of Allah, and no other color. Under the shade of this banner, the Arabs attained ascendancy. They became the leaders of the world, and their leadership was the leadership of goodness. It was a strong leadership, a wise leadership, and a leadership successful in every respect. This achievement was successful for the first time in Arab history, and in human history as well the Islamic revolution was a remarkable success for humanity.

Maulana Abul Hasan Ali Nadwi, in the chapter "Islamic Rule and Muslim Leaders" of his well-known book *The Impact of the Rise and Fall of Muslims on the Human World*, says:

"The Muslims came onto the stage. They took the reins of guidance of the world into their own hands and removed from that position of leadership those sick nations which had seized it and which they had never used properly. The Muslims took all the people of the world with them and began to lead them with balance and correct pace toward their true destination. They possessed all those qualities that proved them worthy of the lofty office of guiding all nations, and under their oversight and leadership they guaranteed the welfare and felicity of peoples. What were these distinctive qualities? They are the following:

(1) They possessed the Heavenly Book and the law of God. They did not make legislation or laws of their own, because human legislation is the source of ignorance, oppression and errors, and when human beings make laws for human beings, they are amended and altered every day, whereas heavenly books are protected from these errors. The Muslims were safe from groping blindly and flailing in darkness in their daily affairs, in politics and in leadership. They had the light of divine revelation to walk by, through which all the paths and turns of life were illuminated for them. Every step they took fell in light, and they could see their goal clearly. In Surah al-An'am (6:122) it is said:

﴿Is one who was dead and We gave him life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people like one who is in darkness, unable to emerge from it?﴾

They possessed a divine law and shariah according to which they judged among people. They were made standard-bearers of truth and justice, and even in the most severe provocation, anger, enmity and hatred, they were commanded not to abandon truthfulness and justice, and not to let it happen that they would take revenge in matters of truth and justice:

﴿O you who believe, be persistently standing firm for Allah, witnesses in justice, and do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness. And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾ (5:8)

(2) They had attained the position of government and leadership after firm moral training and the refinement of the self. They did not leap from lowliness to loftiness with all their moral defects and faults, as the ordinary ruling nations and governing people of the world do. Rather, for a long period divine revelation had been reforming and training them, and for years they had been under the complete oversight and teaching of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He purified them and fully trained them. He accustomed them to a life of asceticism and piety, and he made them habituated to chastity and trustworthiness, to selflessness and sacrifice, and to the fear of Allah. He completely removed greed for rule and office from their hearts. His saying was: 'By Allah, we will not entrust any office to a person who asks for it or who desires it.' Their hearts were completely cleansed of the desire for elevation, grandeur and honor, and the desire for turmoil and corruption. In their ears, day and night, these words of the Qur'an resounded:

﴿That is the Home of the Hereafter We assign to those who do not desire haughtiness upon the earth or corruption, and the best outcome is for the righteous﴾ (28:83)."

Therefore they did not rush to accept positions and offices of government; on the contrary, they avoided accepting them, and they would tremble at the thought of their responsibilities. Whenever any one of them was offered a post, he would hold back and did not consider himself fit to bear that burden, let alone that any of them would put forward his own name for government or campaign for his own person. Then, when they took up a responsibility, they did not regard it as spoils of war or a morsel of sweet gain, but considered it a trust (amanah) upon them and a trial from Allah. They believed that they had to appear before Allah and answer for every small and great matter. And they always recited this verse:

﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their owners and, when you judge between people, to judge with justice﴾ (4:58). "O Muslims, Allah commands you to deliver trusts to those entitled to them, and when you make judgment among people, to judge with justice." Also this verse:

﴿And it is He who has made you successors upon the earth and raised some of you above others in degrees, to test you in what He has given you. Indeed, your Lord is swift in penalty, and indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (6:165).

(3) They were not servants of any nation, nor representatives of any race or homeland whose sole concern was the prosperity of that nation or race, nor did they believe in the superiority of one nation, granting it leadership and dominance over all nations, holding the belief that "our nation is meant to lead, while other nations are meant only to be subjugated." They did not emerge beyond the bounds of the Arab world so that they might establish an Arab empire over the world and live a life of comfort and luxury under its shelter, boasting and showing arrogance over others under its protection. Nor did they go out so that they might free people from the slavery of the Romans and Persians only to enslave them to the Arabs and themselves. They went out only so that they might free the servants of Allah from the servitude of all those who are like themselves and bring them into the service of Allah alone, without partner.

The envoy of the Muslims, Rib'i ibn 'Amir, declared this reality in the full court of Persian King Rustam. He said: "Allah has sent us so that we may bring people out of the servitude of creatures into the worship of the One Allah, and from the narrowness of the world into its vastness, and from the oppression of religions into the justice of Islam." Thus, all the nations and all the people of the world stood on one level in their sight; if there was any distinction, it was only of religion. In short, they fully acted upon the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "All people are the children of Adam, and Adam was made of earth. An Arab has no superiority over a non-Arab, nor a non-Arab over an Arab, except by piety."

And in verse 13 of Surah al-Hujurat:

﴿O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you﴾ (49:13).

On one occasion the son of 'Amr ibn al-'As, the governor of Egypt, struck an Egyptian with a whip and boasted of his father and forefathers. 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) ordered the Egyptian to take retaliation from him, and said to 'Amr ibn al-'As: "Since when have you enslaved people, while their mothers bore them free?"

These conquerors and rulers never showed stinginess or narrow-mindedness in bestowing religion, knowledge and civilization, and in matters of government and offices of government they never considered nationality or colour and race. Rather, they were a cloud of generosity that encompassed the whole world, and its bounty was common to all. It watered the entire world, every part of the earth prayed for it, and creatures benefited from it according to their capacity and ability.

Under the shelter and rule of these people, all the nations of the world, without distinction of colour, homeland, religion, knowledge, civilization or government, were given the full opportunity to take their full share and to participate with the Arabs in the reconstruction. Indeed, many of their individuals surpassed the Arabs in many excellences, and among them arose imams, jurists and muhaddithin who were themselves the crown of the Arabs and the pride of the Muslims.

(4) Man is a composite of body, heart and intellect. A person cannot attain true success and felicity, and humanity cannot attain balanced progress, unless all these faculties of man develop and are nurtured in a proportionate manner befitting his station. A sound civilization cannot exist in the world unless there is established a religious, moral, intellectual and material environment of this kind, in which it is possible for man to reach perfection with full ease. Experience has proven that this is not possible unless the guidance of life and the steering of civilization are in the hands of those who believe in both spirituality and materiality, who are perfect examples of religious and moral life, and who are endowed with sound reason and correct knowledge. (pp. 100–164)

And in another section, under the heading of the Rightly Guided Caliphate era, he writes:

"Thus, in history we know of no period more complete and successful in all these respects than the era of the Rightly Guided Caliphate. In that era, spiritual, moral, religious and scholarly resources, and the means of producing the perfect human being and a sound civilization, were helpers of one another. In that government, which was counted among the greatest governments of the world, with a political and material power that surpassed all contemporary powers, high moral examples and high standards were the rule. Along with commerce and industry, morality and virtue were also at their full height. Along with the expansion of conquests and the progress of civilization, the progress of both morality and utility also continued. Thus, despite the extraordinary vastness of the Islamic state, the extreme growth of population, and the incentives of the means and causes of luxury, incidents of crime and immorality occurred very rarely. The relationship of an individual with another individual, and of the community with its members, was astonishing. This was a standard era, which a person of a more developed era could not even dream of, and a more blessed and flourishing age cannot even be imagined." (p. 167)

These were some features of that blessed era in which humanity lived, for a brief span, under the Islamic constitution set forth by Surah al-'Asr: in that period people were ruled by a community of faith, of such men, who had raised the banners of faith, took righteous deeds as their program, and made the counsel of truth and the exhortation to patience their emblem.

This was a golden era, which cannot be compared with the ruin from which all of humanity today suffers. In the struggle between good and evil, all of humanity is afflicted with loss and destruction. Humanity has closed its eyes to that great good which once the Arabs were the leaders and guides of all humanity; and in the later periods, when they threw down these banners, they became servants of the caravan of humanity, while this caravan too is advancing toward the station of ruin, and in the end the condition has come about that humanity has picked up satanic banners, and none of them is a human banner. Humanity has picked up the banners of falsehood; nowhere is a banner of truth visible. Humanity has picked up the banners of blindness and misguidance; in them nowhere is a single banner of guidance and light visible. All banners are banners of loss; not a single banner of success is visible. The banner of Allah, by which the Arabs once overspread the world, is still present today. This banner still awaits a hand to raise it. There is need of some one community or nation which will walk on the path of goodness, guidance, reform and salvation under this banner.

This is the story of gain and loss in this world. This worldly greatness is a great success in its own place, but if we compare it with the success of the Hereafter, it is very insignificant. The real gain and loss is that of the Hereafter; true gain and loss are there, because that is the long life, the everlasting life, and the eternal abode. The real profit and the real loss are there: Paradise, the profit of Allah's pleasure, or Hell, the loss of Allah's displeasure. In the Hereafter, where a person may have reached his highest development and perfection, or may have progressed to such an extent that he has lost his humanity, he will fall to the value of a stone, and in comfort and rest he will be less than a stone.

﴿On the Day when a man will look upon what his hands have sent forward, and the disbeliever will say, "I wish I were dust!"﴾ (78:40).

The truth is that this surah presents a decisive and clear-cut path of truth; it shows that all paths are paths of loss, except:

﴿Except for those who believed and did righteous deeds and advised one another to truth and advised one another to patience﴾ (103:3).

This is one path, and there is no plurality in it; it is the path of faith and righteous deeds, the path of establishing an Islamic community, the path of a community which counsels the truth and enjoins goodness, which is the ink of truthfulness and whose wages are patience.

The truth is that the path is one. That is why, whenever two companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) met each other, they would not part until they had recited Surah al-'Asr; after that they would greet each other with salaam and depart. In fact, they would make a mutual pledge that they would follow this revolutionary constitution; they would agree among themselves that they would remain on the path of faithful reform, continue to counsel the truth and enjoin patience, and would pledge that they would remain guardians of this constitution and members of the community that follows this constitution.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 103, verses 1–3 (part 1 of 3)

The question is: what is faith (iman)? .... We do not give a jurisprudential (fiqhi) explanation or definition of faith here. Our discussion is limited to the temperament of faith, its worth and value, and its effects on life.

Faith is in fact the bond that this small, limited, human creature establishes with the Reality that is eternal, everlasting and enduring, which is the origin of this universe and from which this universe came into existence. For this reason, this human creature is also connected to the universe, in that both have one Creator. Then this human being is connected to the laws of nature according to which this world operates, and the human being is connected to the forces that are active in this universe. The human being steps out of the shell of his own petty and limited self and enters into the vastness of the universe. Thus he goes beyond the boundaries of his limited power and enters the "limitless powers" that exist within this universe. This universe is so vast in comparison to the human being that its very boundaries lie beyond human knowledge. Then the human being steps out of the circle of his limited lifespan and enters the limitless times of the existence and the times that come after the Resurrection.

This bond of human creation, which grants strength, vastness and freedom, also grants him the taste to enjoy this entire universe and the beauty found within it, and to see the creatures that love his soul. Because of this bond, the brief journey of life becomes a journey of recreation for the human being, or becomes a tour of an exhibition that Allah has adorned for this human being in every place, every location and every era. The truth is that this is a very great good fortune, a supreme level of joy and recreation, and a friendship with this entire universe. It is a wealth compared to which no other wealth has any value. It is also a loss such that if someone is deprived of it, there is no greater loss or deficit than that.

Furthermore, the basic elements of faith are also those that are the basic constituent elements of humanity:

(1) Through the servitude of one God, a person is freed from all obedience, servitude and worship other than the One God. In this way, a sense arises within people that all servants have one standing and are equal with one another. Therefore, it is not a reasonable attitude that a person should be granted the true blessing of freedom! This is the freedom that springs from the human conscience and springs from the concept that exists as a fact and reality, and that concept is that in this universe there is only one real power and one real object of worship. Accordingly, the natural demand of this conception of life and conception of the universe is that the human being be free, and the logical outcome of this belief is also that the human being be free.

(2) A person develops Rabbaniyyah (a state of being devoted to the Lord), and he derives all his concepts, all his values and standards, all his priorities, and his entire constitution and law from Allah. His relations with Allah, with this universe, and with people are established in accordance with Allah's commands and laws. His personal desires and personal interests disappear from his life, and in their place Allah's Shariah (law) and justice take over. In the consciousness of the believer, the worth and value of his system of life rises, and his personality is elevated above the concepts and values of Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance, pre-Islamic paganism). Jahili priorities come to an end, and all the bonds that are based on the earth, this world and material concepts come to an end. Even if this person is an individual, because a believing individual also takes his concepts, his values and his priorities directly from Allah, since these values are indeed more exalted, more honourable, and more beneficial and deserving of regard.

(3) As a result of faith, the relationship between the Creator and the creation is also determined. The station of divinity and servitude, of lordship and bondage, is also determined, and this relationship comes forth clear and pure. This relationship, which connects a mortal human being to an immortal Being, is determined and made clear in a very simple and understandable manner, and in this path the human being no longer needs any intermediary. Through the clarification of ranks, light arises in the heart and tranquility in the soul. Love and trust arise in the human self. Anxiety, fear, distress and restlessness come to an end. Through this clarity of ranks, a person neither commits unjust arrogance, nor, by fabricating falsehoods and relying on invented concepts, claims for himself a superior station over other human beings.

(4) Because of faith, the People of Faith are granted steadfastness upon the Islamic system of life. Therefore, goodness among believers is not a temporary matter, nor an accidental, isolated incident. Rather, the Islamic system is an event that has real causes and has certain real objectives, and those who run the Islamic system are people bound together fi Allah (for the sake of Allah), who support one another. From such people a sound community is formed, which has one single purpose and one distinguished banner. This community is a historical community, and its past generations are also connected to the coming generations, and the coming generations are connected to the past, and this connection is a strong connection.

(5) As a result of this, a concept arises among people that the human being is extremely honoured. The human being rises in his own eyes, and in the conscience of the believer there is established the modesty that he should not do any action as a result of which he would fall from the rank to which Allah has raised him. This is that exalted and lofty station which no human being could even imagine reaching, that he is honoured in the sight of Allah. Every religion or philosophical concept that lowers a human being in his own eyes and declares him to be a contemptible creature, which was created in a manner that is regarded as a later addition, actually creates a distance between the human being and the higher realm. Such a religion or philosophy lowers the human being and leads him towards degradation, even if it does not say this explicitly.

Thus, the philosophies of Darwin and Freud and the Marxist system were the worst philosophies and systems, which afflicted humanity with the worst calamity and gave it a wrong direction from the standpoint of humanity, human nature and humanity itself, and made it believe that every degradation, every filth and every contempt is in fact a natural and necessary part of human life. This is not something to be surprised at, and therefore there is nothing to be ashamed of in it. Thus these philosophies and systems are in fact a heinous crime against humanity and deserve to be hated. (Sayyid, are you not aware that all the idols of Marxism have been toppled from the socialist world?)

(6) The mere concept that a human being is an honoured creature in the sight of Allah purifies and cleanses human consciousness. Then the concept that Allah is the Overseer of all, and that He knows what is in the breasts, also purifies human consciousness. A sound-natured human being, whose nature has not been distorted by the writings of people like Karl Marx and Freud, is ashamed that another human being like himself should become aware of the secrets of his heart and his evil thoughts. And a true believer, who holds the conviction that Allah is aware of all the secrets and hidden things in his breast, trembles at the thought that these and these thoughts exist in his heart. Through this he cleanses his consciousness and his feelings, and also purifies his heart.

The truth is that the moment faith arises, a moral beauty arises within the human being. He believes that there is one God who is just, merciful, generous and forgiving, forbearing and loving. He does not like evil, He likes goodness. He knows the treachery of the eyes and is the Knower of the secrets of hearts.

(7) Then there is the concept that the human being has been granted freedom of will, and at the same time he is being fully observed by Allah. As a result, awareness and alertness arise within the person, and the understanding and reflection that arise from this lead the human being to adopt a responsible attitude, both regarding himself and regarding other human beings. This responsibility is before Allah. Therefore, when a believer performs any action, his awareness and consciousness is that in every matter and at every step he thinks in his heart and considers the consequences before taking a step. This is because, according to this concept, the human being is a creature who has a position in this world. Therefore, within the order of this universe he is a responsible creature.

(8) Among the important effects of faith is that a believer does not pounce upon the interests of this world in the way that dogs pounce upon bones. Among the indications and effects of faith is that it leads a person to choose that which has lofty purpose in the sight of Allah, and which is "good" and enduring.

﴿And for this let the competitors compete﴾ (26:83). "Let those who wish to compete compete in goodness." Competition in the rewards that are with Allah lifts a person above this world, purifies his heart, and the person becomes clean and pure. Moreover, through this the sphere of a believer's activities becomes broader. He goes beyond the borders of this world and is active in the Hereafter as well. Alongside the earth, he also displays his vigour in the higher realm. This very thing creates in him the strength to continue doing good without concern for results, or not to be hasty about results. This is because he seeks goodness because it is goodness, and because the will of Allah is such. It is not his responsibility that the results of goodness should emerge within this small, limited lifespan. This is because the Allah for whose sake this goodness is being done is Living; He does not die. He does not forget, and He is not unaware of anything. Furthermore, this world is not the true abode of recompense, and all accounts are not settled in this world alone. Therefore, the believer seeks help to keep goodness flowing from a spring that never dries up, and this is why the movement of goodness continues. This is not a momentary enthusiasm, nor an individual incident. It is this faithful spirit which creates in a believer such strength that he stands up against the greatest of evils, whether this evil takes the form of a single dictator and tyrant, or the pressure of Jahili concepts and priorities, or the form of the desires of the self. This individual pressure falls upon a person in such a way that he thinks that this world is brief, that life is short, and that one should indulge in pleasures within it:

"Babur, live in pleasure, for the world is not repeated." (Babur ba-aish kosh, ki alam dobara nist.)

Or he thinks that it is so brief that good deeds cannot bear their results within it, and that we do not see any chance of seeing the triumph of truth over falsehood. Therefore faith treats this condition, and treats it at its very root.

The truth is that faith alone is the foundation of life and the root of life, and from it all the branches of goodness spring forth, and every fruit of it hangs from these roots. If faith is absent, it is as if the root of a tree has been cut, and all its branches will wither and dry up. And if they do not dry up, then they will be a satanic fruit, and it will not attain permanence or growth.

The truth is that faith is the centre and axis to which all the strings of a higher life are connected, and if faith is absent, life becomes a disconnected movement, and without faith this life has no stability or repose. Desires and inclinations pull a person wherever they go, carrying him away.

Faith is in fact a system, and because of it all the scattered deeds become connected with one another, and because of it these deeds come into harmony with one another. They come to be in one direction, having one movement, one motive, and one target.

It is for this reason that the Holy Quran declares null and void every deed that is not based upon this principle, that does not revolve around this axis, and that does not spring from the fountainhead of faith. The Islamic ideology of life and the Islamic system of beliefs are completely open and explicit in this matter. In Surah Ibrahim it is said:

﴿The likeness of those who disbelieved in their Lord is that their deeds are like ashes, which the wind blows violently on a stormy day. They will not be able to obtain anything of what they have earned﴾ (18:14). And in Surah Nur it is said:

﴿As for those who disbelieved, their deeds are like a mirage in a level desert, which the thirsty one thinks to be water, until when he comes to it he finds it to be nothing﴾ (39:24).

These texts clearly indicate that deeds, as long as they are not based upon faith, have no worth or value in Islam. Beneath deeds there must be the motive that the Creator of the universe has commanded them, and their purpose must be to be in harmony with the creation of this universe. This is the logical outcome of the belief that returns all matters to Allah. Therefore, any deed that has been severed from faith loses its meaning and value.

(Ustad Muhammad Abduh, under the verse ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ (8:99), wrote: "Some scholars have recorded a consensus (ijma') that no good deed of a disbeliever will benefit him on the Day of Resurrection, and his punishment will not be lightened; but this is a fundamental matter." We believe that this question is not one of consensus, but one of the explicit texts of the Quran, and the Quran and Sunnah are completely clear in this matter.) (Sayyid Qutb)

**Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran) on Surah 103, verses 1–3 (part 2 of 3)**

Faith is evidence that the believer's nature is sound, the structure of his personality is intact and whole, and he moves in harmony with this entire universe. The natural order that exists in his environment is in accord with him, and therefore he lives within this universe. Every believer whose personality is sound has a harmony with the universe, and this harmony and unity is the fruit of faith alone. The universe contains signs and indications that show that one and the same hand of power is the Creator of the cosmos. Therefore, if this harmony between a person and the universe is broken, it is evidence that his personality has been disturbed and that the capacity by which he draws lessons and signs from the universe has been lost. Because of this corruption, the person will remain in loss. Even if some of his deeds appear to bear the mark of goodness, without faith these deeds will not be accepted.... In short, the world of the believer is broad, comprehensive, long-reaching, elevated, beautiful and successful. In contrast, the world of those who are not believers is small, base, low, weak, hopeless and wretched, and its outcome and end is loss and failure.

﴿And do righteous deeds﴾ (3:103). Righteous deeds are in truth the natural fruit of faith. When faith settles in a heart, righteous action becomes its inherent movement, just as the heart is in constant motion. Faith is therefore a dynamic and positive movement. As soon as it takes its seat in a personality, it appears in the form of righteous action. From the Islamic point of view, faith is exactly like this. Islam does not recognize a faith that is extinguished and produces no movement, a faith that is hidden and does not come out of the believer's being in living form. If there is no such natural movement within it, that faith is counterfeit and dead. Faith is a flower whose fragrance cannot be stopped; wherever there is a flower, its fragrance will continue to spread. And if a person has no scent of faith, it is as though he does not exist.

From this it becomes clear that faith is the name of movement, action and construction, and all these matters come from Allah. Faith contains no contraction; it is not a negative thing. It does not settle in the hidden folds of the conscience. Faith is not the name of good wishes that are not backed by any movement. This is the open temperament of Islam, which makes Islam a superior constructive force, and this power is the central driving force within practical life.

This is the meaning of the principle that faith must be connected with the Islamic system of life. The Islamic system of life is a continuous movement that is taking place throughout this entire universe. This movement has been created by a governing power, it has a purpose, and handing leadership of humanity to faith means bringing into being a leadership that establishes a method of movement in accordance with the temperament of this entire universe. In other words, it means establishing a good, pure and constructive struggle that is worthy of the system of life that has come from Allah.

﴿And who enjoin one another to truth and enjoin one another to patience﴾ (3:103). Through the acts of enjoining truth and enjoining patience, the features of the Muslim ummah (community) become clearly visible. The organized community (jama'ah muslimah) is also established along the lines of the Muslim ummah. It has a distinct existence and personality. Its members have a distinctive bond among them. All people share one direction. This ummah or community is also conscious of its own existence, and its duties are before it. This ummah knows what it must do in relation to faith and righteous action. It knows that from the standpoint of faith and righteous action it must also lead all of humanity. Therefore, to counsel one another to truth means that you must rise up carrying the Great Trust (amanat kubra).

In short, from the word "tawasi" (mutual counsel and exhortation), and from its meaning, its character and its reality, the existence of the Muslim ummah emerges, or the concept of a united community arises. That is, an ummah that is distinguished, wise, and responsible for establishing truth, goodness, and justice upon this earth. Thus this is the most sublime and beautiful picture of the Muslim ummah. Islam desires such an ummah: a distinguished, strong, wise community that watches over truth and goodness, whose members constantly counsel one another to truth and exhort one another to patience, live together in love and cooperation, and among whom a special brotherhood prevails, which the Qur'an expresses as mutual counsel.

Enjoining truth is necessary because carrying the truth is a difficult task. In this world there are countless factors that lead a person away from the path of truth: carnal desires, expediency, national and family notions, the oppression of rebels and dictators, the injustice of wrongdoers, the transgressions of those who exceed limits, and so on. When people counsel one another, in essence a reminder takes place. People's resolve grows, and in terms of aims and objectives, unity and oneness arise among the members of the community. And in taking up responsibilities, in essence one bears the burden of another. Through counsel, all individual tendencies are gathered together and multiplied many times over, and those who are the guardians and supporters of truth feel that they are not alone. In the work of protecting truth and reality, there are others with me. They counsel him, encourage him, love him, and stand behind him, and they will never let him be humiliated. This religion is indeed the truth, and only a community can protect this religion, one that is mutually known, mutually responsible, mutually supportive, and that makes up for one another's weaknesses.

Enjoining patience is also very necessary, because remaining on the path of faith and righteous action and watching over truth and justice is a difficult task. It requires patience, perseverance, and fierce struggle against the factors within the self, and it also requires struggle against the factors outside the self. It requires endurance and hardship in the face of difficulties that arise on this path. Likewise, it requires patience in the face of the arrogance and pride of falsehood, patience over the length of the road, patience over the slowness of success, and patience when the signs of the path become obscure and vanish.

Enjoining patience increases human strength and produces a collective consciousness among people, that all of us have one goal and one direction. In this way everyone receives support. Workers, while laboring on this path, become close and intimate with one another, and they advance with great determination, steadfastness, and insistence upon their aim. Furthermore, through this several other collective qualities also come into being, and these are necessary for the stability of the Islamic community, because Islam cannot live without a communal atmosphere. Islam also manifests itself in the form of a society. If there is no society, there will be no Islam, and that would be sheer loss.

The Qur'an has established for us a constitution according to which a society is declared successful and protected from worldly and otherworldly loss. If we examine the present condition of the world through the lens of this constitution, we will see before us this frightful picture of the world: that the whole world is at present in complete loss. The more frightening aspect of this loss is that, even before the Hereafter, we have already fallen into severe loss from a purely worldly standpoint. We see that humanity has completely turned away from that goodness whose blessings Allah had made universal for mankind. Furthermore, that sovereign authority which is faithful and Islamic, which is founded upon goodness and the principles of truth and justice, has disappeared from this world. The most ugly aspect of this picture is that Muslims, or more precisely, those people who were far from goodness and virtue in comparison with other human beings who dwell on this earth, have moved far away from the system of life that Allah had chosen for them. They have trampled underfoot the constitution and law that Allah had prescribed for them, which Allah had declared to be the only path to salvation from loss and failure. Especially those lands from which the banners of goodness were first raised have themselves brought down the banners that Allah had raised for them. These were the banners of faith. And the most unfortunate thing is that the lands from which the banners of Allah's religion were raised have adopted racial nationalism, although the history of this earth bears witness that no people has ever attained goodness through racial nationalism. The nationalism (Arab nationalism) whose banners these people have raised existed before Islam as well, but because of it they neither accomplished any notable achievement on this earth, nor was any achievement of theirs recorded in the heavens. When Islam came, through the Arabs it raised a banner that was purely the banner of Allah. No other element shared in it. It was in the name of Allah, and no one shared in that name. It was attributed only to Allah, with no other attribution. It bore only the color of Allah, and no other color. Under the shade of this banner, the Arabs attained ascendancy. They became the leaders of the world, and their leadership was the leadership of goodness. It was a strong leadership, a wise leadership, and a leadership successful in every respect. This achievement was successful for the first time in Arab history, and in human history as well the Islamic revolution was a remarkable success for humanity.

Maulana Abul Hasan Ali Nadwi, in the chapter "Islamic Rule and Muslim Leaders" of his well-known book *The Impact of the Rise and Fall of Muslims on the Human World*, says:

"The Muslims came onto the stage. They took the reins of guidance of the world into their own hands and removed from that position of leadership those sick nations which had seized it and which they had never used properly. The Muslims took all the people of the world with them and began to lead them with balance and correct pace toward their true destination. They possessed all those qualities that proved them worthy of the lofty office of guiding all nations, and under their oversight and leadership they guaranteed the welfare and felicity of peoples. What were these distinctive qualities? They are the following:

(1) They possessed the Heavenly Book and the law of God. They did not make legislation or laws of their own, because human legislation is the source of ignorance, oppression and errors, and when human beings make laws for human beings, they are amended and altered every day, whereas heavenly books are protected from these errors. The Muslims were safe from groping blindly and flailing in darkness in their daily affairs, in politics and in leadership. They had the light of divine revelation to walk by, through which all the paths and turns of life were illuminated for them. Every step they took fell in light, and they could see their goal clearly. In Surah al-An'am (6:122) it is said:

﴿Is one who was dead and We gave him life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people like one who is in darkness, unable to emerge from it?﴾

They possessed a divine law and shariah according to which they judged among people. They were made standard-bearers of truth and justice, and even in the most severe provocation, anger, enmity and hatred, they were commanded not to abandon truthfulness and justice, and not to let it happen that they would take revenge in matters of truth and justice:

﴿O you who believe, be persistently standing firm for Allah, witnesses in justice, and do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness. And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾ (5:8)

(2) They had attained the position of government and leadership after firm moral training and the refinement of the self. They did not leap from lowliness to loftiness with all their moral defects and faults, as the ordinary ruling nations and governing people of the world do. Rather, for a long period divine revelation had been reforming and training them, and for years they had been under the complete oversight and teaching of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He purified them and fully trained them. He accustomed them to a life of asceticism and piety, and he made them habituated to chastity and trustworthiness, to selflessness and sacrifice, and to the fear of Allah. He completely removed greed for rule and office from their hearts. His saying was: 'By Allah, we will not entrust any office to a person who asks for it or who desires it.' Their hearts were completely cleansed of the desire for elevation, grandeur and honor, and the desire for turmoil and corruption. In their ears, day and night, these words of the Qur'an resounded:

﴿That is the Home of the Hereafter We assign to those who do not desire haughtiness upon the earth or corruption, and the best outcome is for the righteous﴾ (28:83)."

Therefore they did not rush to accept positions and offices of government; on the contrary, they avoided accepting them, and they would tremble at the thought of their responsibilities. Whenever any one of them was offered a post, he would hold back and did not consider himself fit to bear that burden, let alone that any of them would put forward his own name for government or campaign for his own person. Then, when they took up a responsibility, they did not regard it as spoils of war or a morsel of sweet gain, but considered it a trust (amanah) upon them and a trial from Allah. They believed that they had to appear before Allah and answer for every small and great matter. And they always recited this verse:

﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their owners and, when you judge between people, to judge with justice﴾ (4:58). "O Muslims, Allah commands you to deliver trusts to those entitled to them, and when you make judgment among people, to judge with justice." Also this verse:

﴿And it is He who has made you successors upon the earth and raised some of you above others in degrees, to test you in what He has given you. Indeed, your Lord is swift in penalty, and indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (6:165).

(3) They were not servants of any nation, nor representatives of any race or homeland whose sole concern was the prosperity of that nation or race, nor did they believe in the superiority of one nation, granting it leadership and dominance over all nations, holding the belief that "our nation is meant to lead, while other nations are meant only to be subjugated." They did not emerge beyond the bounds of the Arab world so that they might establish an Arab empire over the world and live a life of comfort and luxury under its shelter, boasting and showing arrogance over others under its protection. Nor did they go out so that they might free people from the slavery of the Romans and Persians only to enslave them to the Arabs and themselves. They went out only so that they might free the servants of Allah from the servitude of all those who are like themselves and bring them into the service of Allah alone, without partner.

The envoy of the Muslims, Rib'i ibn 'Amir, declared this reality in the full court of Persian King Rustam. He said: "Allah has sent us so that we may bring people out of the servitude of creatures into the worship of the One Allah, and from the narrowness of the world into its vastness, and from the oppression of religions into the justice of Islam." Thus, all the nations and all the people of the world stood on one level in their sight; if there was any distinction, it was only of religion. In short, they fully acted upon the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "All people are the children of Adam, and Adam was made of earth. An Arab has no superiority over a non-Arab, nor a non-Arab over an Arab, except by piety."

And in verse 13 of Surah al-Hujurat:

﴿O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you﴾ (49:13).

On one occasion the son of 'Amr ibn al-'As, the governor of Egypt, struck an Egyptian with a whip and boasted of his father and forefathers. 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) ordered the Egyptian to take retaliation from him, and said to 'Amr ibn al-'As: "Since when have you enslaved people, while their mothers bore them free?"

These conquerors and rulers never showed stinginess or narrow-mindedness in bestowing religion, knowledge and civilization, and in matters of government and offices of government they never considered nationality or colour and race. Rather, they were a cloud of generosity that encompassed the whole world, and its bounty was common to all. It watered the entire world, every part of the earth prayed for it, and creatures benefited from it according to their capacity and ability.

Under the shelter and rule of these people, all the nations of the world, without distinction of colour, homeland, religion, knowledge, civilization or government, were given the full opportunity to take their full share and to participate with the Arabs in the reconstruction. Indeed, many of their individuals surpassed the Arabs in many excellences, and among them arose imams, jurists and muhaddithin who were themselves the crown of the Arabs and the pride of the Muslims.

(4) Man is a composite of body, heart and intellect. A person cannot attain true success and felicity, and humanity cannot attain balanced progress, unless all these faculties of man develop and are nurtured in a proportionate manner befitting his station. A sound civilization cannot exist in the world unless there is established a religious, moral, intellectual and material environment of this kind, in which it is possible for man to reach perfection with full ease. Experience has proven that this is not possible unless the guidance of life and the steering of civilization are in the hands of those who believe in both spirituality and materiality, who are perfect examples of religious and moral life, and who are endowed with sound reason and correct knowledge. (pp. 100–164)

And in another section, under the heading of the Rightly Guided Caliphate era, he writes:

"Thus, in history we know of no period more complete and successful in all these respects than the era of the Rightly Guided Caliphate. In that era, spiritual, moral, religious and scholarly resources, and the means of producing the perfect human being and a sound civilization, were helpers of one another. In that government, which was counted among the greatest governments of the world, with a political and material power that surpassed all contemporary powers, high moral examples and high standards were the rule. Along with commerce and industry, morality and virtue were also at their full height. Along with the expansion of conquests and the progress of civilization, the progress of both morality and utility also continued. Thus, despite the extraordinary vastness of the Islamic state, the extreme growth of population, and the incentives of the means and causes of luxury, incidents of crime and immorality occurred very rarely. The relationship of an individual with another individual, and of the community with its members, was astonishing. This was a standard era, which a person of a more developed era could not even dream of, and a more blessed and flourishing age cannot even be imagined." (p. 167)

These were some features of that blessed era in which humanity lived, for a brief span, under the Islamic constitution set forth by Surah al-'Asr: in that period people were ruled by a community of faith, of such men, who had raised the banners of faith, took righteous deeds as their program, and made the counsel of truth and the exhortation to patience their emblem.

This was a golden era, which cannot be compared with the ruin from which all of humanity today suffers. In the struggle between good and evil, all of humanity is afflicted with loss and destruction. Humanity has closed its eyes to that great good which once the Arabs were the leaders and guides of all humanity; and in the later periods, when they threw down these banners, they became servants of the caravan of humanity, while this caravan too is advancing toward the station of ruin, and in the end the condition has come about that humanity has picked up satanic banners, and none of them is a human banner. Humanity has picked up the banners of falsehood; nowhere is a banner of truth visible. Humanity has picked up the banners of blindness and misguidance; in them nowhere is a single banner of guidance and light visible. All banners are banners of loss; not a single banner of success is visible. The banner of Allah, by which the Arabs once overspread the world, is still present today. This banner still awaits a hand to raise it. There is need of some one community or nation which will walk on the path of goodness, guidance, reform and salvation under this banner.

This is the story of gain and loss in this world. This worldly greatness is a great success in its own place, but if we compare it with the success of the Hereafter, it is very insignificant. The real gain and loss is that of the Hereafter; true gain and loss are there, because that is the long life, the everlasting life, and the eternal abode. The real profit and the real loss are there: Paradise, the profit of Allah's pleasure, or Hell, the loss of Allah's displeasure. In the Hereafter, where a person may have reached his highest development and perfection, or may have progressed to such an extent that he has lost his humanity, he will fall to the value of a stone, and in comfort and rest he will be less than a stone.

﴿On the Day when a man will look upon what his hands have sent forward, and the disbeliever will say, "I wish I were dust!"﴾ (78:40).

The truth is that this surah presents a decisive and clear-cut path of truth; it shows that all paths are paths of loss, except:

﴿Except for those who believed and did righteous deeds and advised one another to truth and advised one another to patience﴾ (103:3).

This is one path, and there is no plurality in it; it is the path of faith and righteous deeds, the path of establishing an Islamic community, the path of a community which counsels the truth and enjoins goodness, which is the ink of truthfulness and whose wages are patience.

The truth is that the path is one. That is why, whenever two companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) met each other, they would not part until they had recited Surah al-'Asr; after that they would greet each other with salaam and depart. In fact, they would make a mutual pledge that they would follow this revolutionary constitution; they would agree among themselves that they would remain on the path of faithful reform, continue to counsel the truth and enjoin patience, and would pledge that they would remain guardians of this constitution and members of the community that follows this constitution.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 103, verses 1–3 (part 1 of 3)

The question is: what is faith (iman)? .... We do not give a jurisprudential (fiqhi) explanation or definition of faith here. Our discussion is limited to the temperament of faith, its worth and value, and its effects on life.

Faith is in fact the bond that this small, limited, human creature establishes with the Reality that is eternal, everlasting and enduring, which is the origin of this universe and from which this universe came into existence. For this reason, this human creature is also connected to the universe, in that both have one Creator. Then this human being is connected to the laws of nature according to which this world operates, and the human being is connected to the forces that are active in this universe. The human being steps out of the shell of his own petty and limited self and enters into the vastness of the universe. Thus he goes beyond the boundaries of his limited power and enters the "limitless powers" that exist within this universe. This universe is so vast in comparison to the human being that its very boundaries lie beyond human knowledge. Then the human being steps out of the circle of his limited lifespan and enters the limitless times of the existence and the times that come after the Resurrection.

This bond of human creation, which grants strength, vastness and freedom, also grants him the taste to enjoy this entire universe and the beauty found within it, and to see the creatures that love his soul. Because of this bond, the brief journey of life becomes a journey of recreation for the human being, or becomes a tour of an exhibition that Allah has adorned for this human being in every place, every location and every era. The truth is that this is a very great good fortune, a supreme level of joy and recreation, and a friendship with this entire universe. It is a wealth compared to which no other wealth has any value. It is also a loss such that if someone is deprived of it, there is no greater loss or deficit than that.

Furthermore, the basic elements of faith are also those that are the basic constituent elements of humanity:

(1) Through the servitude of one God, a person is freed from all obedience, servitude and worship other than the One God. In this way, a sense arises within people that all servants have one standing and are equal with one another. Therefore, it is not a reasonable attitude that a person should be granted the true blessing of freedom! This is the freedom that springs from the human conscience and springs from the concept that exists as a fact and reality, and that concept is that in this universe there is only one real power and one real object of worship. Accordingly, the natural demand of this conception of life and conception of the universe is that the human being be free, and the logical outcome of this belief is also that the human being be free.

(2) A person develops Rabbaniyyah (a state of being devoted to the Lord), and he derives all his concepts, all his values and standards, all his priorities, and his entire constitution and law from Allah. His relations with Allah, with this universe, and with people are established in accordance with Allah's commands and laws. His personal desires and personal interests disappear from his life, and in their place Allah's Shariah (law) and justice take over. In the consciousness of the believer, the worth and value of his system of life rises, and his personality is elevated above the concepts and values of Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance, pre-Islamic paganism). Jahili priorities come to an end, and all the bonds that are based on the earth, this world and material concepts come to an end. Even if this person is an individual, because a believing individual also takes his concepts, his values and his priorities directly from Allah, since these values are indeed more exalted, more honourable, and more beneficial and deserving of regard.

(3) As a result of faith, the relationship between the Creator and the creation is also determined. The station of divinity and servitude, of lordship and bondage, is also determined, and this relationship comes forth clear and pure. This relationship, which connects a mortal human being to an immortal Being, is determined and made clear in a very simple and understandable manner, and in this path the human being no longer needs any intermediary. Through the clarification of ranks, light arises in the heart and tranquility in the soul. Love and trust arise in the human self. Anxiety, fear, distress and restlessness come to an end.
